sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Open source your work so you can keep it
sections.para: Ideas are rarely copied. The real advantage of open source is that you keep using your own work: Dinis brought open projects into each job, ran The Cyber Boardroom openly while employed, and continued after leaving. Publish early and rough, tell your managers, and keep it separate.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Nobody copies; you keep it; rough protects you
sections.para: Open sourcing is not about copying risk but continuity. Bring projects into the job, experiment openly with managers aware, publish rough and early, keep separate machines, never compete, and the learning helps the day job.

sections.label: Nobody copies it
sections.line: Ideas need a specific person to happen
sections.para: Dinis's unfollowed open ideas are still there, untaken. A company copying your code still has to decide, fund, staff, deploy and own it: three months at best, closer to a year, by open-source.sgit.ai's estimate.

sections.label: You get to keep using it
sections.line: Closed work stays behind when you leave
sections.para: Work for an employer is usually locked in, so every new job starts from scratch. Bringing open source projects into each company made Dinis more productive there and let his work keep improving between jobs.

sections.label: The Cyber Boardroom
sections.line: The Cyber Boardroom: open, known, and continued
sections.para: An AI experiment run openly while Dinis worked for two companies, with his managers aware. After leaving he continued; it was incorporated about a month later, did not work, and lacked the confidential data store that sgit now provides.

sections.label: Publish early, and rough
sections.line: A rough, early history is your protection
sections.para: Talk about ideas early; the imagined army of critics does not exist. Rough public work shows an employer it is an experiment; something polished from nowhere raises questions and can involve lawyers, while a visible history shows the evolution.

sections.label: Be disciplined
sections.line: Separate machines, and never a competitor
sections.para: Keep side work on separate machines and environments, and never build a direct competitor to your employer.

sections.label: A win for both sides
sections.line: Both sides gain, and the startups follow
sections.para: Learning GenAI on the side made Dinis better at his day job, and the continuity is how he found his startups, three startups later. Funding the time is the next article.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.para: Ideas alone are rarely copied, though projects can be. Read your contract. The Cyber Boardroom did not succeed; the point is continuity, and that managers knew.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: A memo and the open-source site
sections.para: Dinis's memo of 19 October 2026, open-source.sgit.ai's cost-of-copying walkthrough and sgit.ai's not a straight line.
